rationale: Interpreting the boundary execution and recording one source-reasoned refinement of the runtime condition. (1) CheckRun 13b5c712348f412eac6c7ce108a05d91 (exit 0, cases A-D passed) evaluated all seven comparisons completely: the four trim comparisons reproduce the finding (control holds; {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} and {1,3} each violated with valid witnesses 3, 5, 7) and the three new boundary comparisons hold - in every trigger configuration the snapshot call returns ok and moves the compacted index from 0 to 1 exactly where both trim calls made no progress, while in the contiguous control the snapshot is a no-op because trim had already compacted that index. That turns the previously source-derived 'snapshot remains available' caveat into a measured boundary, so I correct the trim knowledge entry under its existing id and append the account for that question. (2) I also re-read the follower-side gating and found a source reason why the runtime defect's condition is exactly one round trip wide: every message that could advance the origin's decided index (AcceptDecide, Decide, AcceptSync) is gated by `check_valid_ballot`, which rejects a ballot above the node's promise, so the origin cannot learn that a different entry occupies the assigned index while it is still promised to the ballot that assigned it; the promise change therefore always precedes the decided advance, and the resolution is `Ok` if and only if no `drain_notifiers` pass runs between the two - consistent with the measured band (2 and 4 ms hold, 8 ms and above violated). I record that as knowledge with its sources.

knowledge.changed_premise: The conditions now carry a measured boundary instead of a source-derived caveat: in each trigger configuration the snapshot path was executed on the same instance after the two trim calls and advanced the compacted index from 0 to 1 while trim could not, and in the contiguous control it was a no-op because trim had already compacted that index. The statement, sources and scope are otherwise unchanged.
knowledge.statement: With a configuration whose largest node id exceeds the number of nodes, the leader cannot advance the compacted index through `trim`. `LeaderState::with` allocates `accepted_indexes` for every id up to the largest one, phantom slots (ids that are not in the configuration) are never written, and `LeaderState::get_min_all_accepted_idx` minimises over that whole vector, so the reduced value is 0 no matter how far the real servers have decided. `SequencePaxos::trim` therefore computes a trim index of 0 for `trim(None)`, `InternalStorage::try_trim(0)` finds nothing to compact and the call returns `Ok(())` while `get_compacted_idx()` is unchanged; `trim(Some(k))` for any k >= 1 fails the guard `idx <= min_all_accepted_idx` and returns `CompactionErr::NotAllDecided(0)`, so the documented repair step ('users can retry with omni_paxos.trim(Some(idx)) which will then succeed') cannot succeed. Measured on real instances with one entry decided by every configured server: {1,2,3} compacted 0 -> 1, while {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} (leader 2, id 1 absent) and the two-node {1,3} each stayed at 0 with `trim_none_result` = ok and `trim_explicit_result` = not_all_decided:0. On the same instances the alternative compaction path still works: `snapshot(Some(decided_idx), true)` returned ok and advanced the compacted index from 0 to 1 in all three trigger configurations, while in the contiguous control it was a no-op because trim had already compacted that index.
knowledge.conditions: Core crate with MemoryStorage, in-process lossless delivery, batch_size 1, majority quorum, one decided entry, leader = first id of each set. The measured trigger is any id set whose largest id exceeds the node count, equivalently any set leaving a phantom slot below the maximum: {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} and {1,3} were executed; sets that are contiguous 1..=n (the control) are unaffected. Snapshot-based compaction is measured to still advance the compacted index under the same trigger, so the defect is confined to the trim path; decision counting is not affected either, because `is_chosen` only counts slots whose accepted index reaches the candidate index and phantom slots hold 0.

knowledge.statement: An origin cannot observe, while still promised to the ballot that assigned its entry an index, that a different entry occupies that index. Every message that could advance the origin's decided index - `AcceptDecide` and `Decide` in `follower.rs`, and `AcceptSync` - is gated by `check_valid_ballot`, which accepts only a message ballot equal to the node's promise and otherwise either sends `NotAccepted` (promise greater) or ignores the message after asking for a re-prepare (promise smaller). The decided index can therefore advance past the assigned index only after the promise has moved to a different ballot, which means the false success of `append_notify` depends on whether a `drain_notifiers` pass runs between the origin's promise change and that decided-index advance - a window of about one round trip, matching the measured band where 2 ms and 4 ms ticks delivered `Superseded` and 8 ms and above delivered `Ok`.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for the origin node of a pending `append_notify` in this actor layer (leader origin or follower origin alike), with the core crate's ballot gating as captured; it does not depend on the quorum size or the batching configuration. It bounds when the `Ok` arm can win, not whether the entry is lost.

investigations.discriminator: Settled: four id sets and seven comparisons, with the snapshot boundary measured. Only same-cause variants remain (contiguous ids starting above 1 in a larger cluster, trimming after part of the log is already snapshotted), which would not change the account.

The condition is now bounded (one round trip) and reasoned from the core's ballot gating as well as measured; what remains open and unmeasured is the follower-origin instance of the same window, which the gating argument covers but no run exercised, plus callers outside this repository.

interpretations.rationale: Current account with the boundary measured. `LeaderState::with` allocates one accepted-index slot per id up to the largest id in the configuration and `LeaderState::get_min_all_accepted_idx` reduces over that vector, so any id set leaving a phantom slot below the maximum pins the reduced value at 0 however far the real servers have decided; `SequencePaxos::trim` compares the caller's index against that value before calling `InternalStorage::try_trim`, which does nothing when the target does not exceed the current compacted index while still returning Ok. The retained execution evaluates seven predicates over four configurations with the same state (every configured server decided the same entry, decided index 1, compacted index 0): the contiguous control `holds` for trim(None) advancing compaction, the three trigger configurations {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} (leader 2, id 1 absent) and the two-node {1,3} are `violated` with valid witnesses 3, 5 and 7 - trim(None) reporting ok with the compacted index unchanged and the documented explicit retry returning `NotAllDecided(0)` - and the three boundary comparisons `hold`: after both trim calls, `snapshot(Some(decided_idx), true)` returns ok and moves the compacted index from 0 to 1 in each trigger configuration, while in the control the snapshot is a no-op because trim had already compacted that index. So the defect is confined to the trim path (snapshotting, the alternative compaction mechanism, still works under the very configuration where trim cannot), and two obligations of the trim API fail together: `trim(None)` reports success without progress, and the documented retry 'users can retry with omni_paxos.trim(Some(idx)) which will then succeed' cannot succeed because the guard demands an index at or below the reduced value of 0. The configuration is admitted by the target's own validation (only more than one node, a non-zero configuration id, valid quorums and that the node set contains this server's pid), and the trigger is a largest id above the node count. Scope is progress of the trim path, not safety: phantom slots hold 0, `is_chosen` counts only slots whose accepted index reaches the candidate index, so decision formation is unaffected.
counterevidence: Trimming is optional compaction: the cluster keeps making progress and the log stays correct, so the defect costs unbounded log growth and a misleading success return rather than lost work.
`try_snapshot` does not consult the reduced value, and the boundary measurement shows it still compacts under every trigger configuration; the defect is confined to the trim path.

The probe used MemoryStorage and a lossless in-process transport, so nothing here speaks to a storage backend that rejects the no-op trim, although the reduced value is computed in the core and does not depend on storage.
The control's explicit retry returned ok without further compaction because the preceding trim(None) had already compacted that index.
limitations: One entry decided, batch_size 1, majority quorum, at most four nodes; larger clusters or longer logs are unmeasured, though the reduced value depends on neither beyond the id range.

The snapshot measurement uses an implemented `Snapshot::create` on a single instance with `local_only = true`; snapshot merging across restarts and the `local_only = false` forwarding path are unmeasured.
The two-node {1,3} case exercises the same reduced value under a different majority rule; no flexible-quorum configuration was tried.
